achievements.Title: Platform Team Charter, Vision & Product Roadmap
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: When the ML Platform team was newly inaugurated with just two engineers, there was no clear ownership model, limited visibility into platform products or golden paths, and no long-term strategic vision to guide how the team operated within DraftKings.
achievements.Action: Drawing on prior platform engineering leadership experience, I partnered with ML Platform leadership (Engineering Manager) and Global Data Platforms leadership (Director) to author the team's inaugural charter, infrastructure product roadmap, SLAs, and RACI charts. I codified a shared-responsibility model anchored in a 'Platform-as-a-Product' operating philosophy so both platform engineers and consuming teams had clear expectations and repeatable golden paths.
achievements.Result: Established the operating foundation that enabled the ML Platform team to scale support to 600+ stakeholders, driving noticeably stronger platform stability and broader adoption of core platform products across the organization.

achievements.Title: Databricks Serverless Compute Enablement
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: ML and data teams needed Databricks Serverless compute to unlock next-generation capabilities—including Online Feature Stores, Databricks Serverless Apps, and MCP—and to run latency-sensitive scheduled workloads whose execution intervals could not tolerate ~5-minute classic cluster spin-ups. However, enabling Serverless required solving private network connectivity between Databricks' isolated serverless compute plane and DraftKings' internal systems while passing rigorous InfoSec review.
achievements.Action: I architected and led the end-to-end Serverless compute enablement using Databricks-native isolation and governance primitives—Network Connectivity Configurations (NCCs), AWS PrivateLink private endpoint rules, network policies, budget policies, service credentials, secret scopes, usage dashboards, and budget alerts—and codified the controls into reusable Terraform modules for repeatable, InfoSec-compliant rollout.
achievements.Result: Cut ad-hoc compute startup latency from ~5 minutes to seconds and unlocked Online Feature Stores, Serverless Apps, and MCP workloads. Adoption scaled rapidly from ~half of ML Platform teams for targeted workloads to an estimated majority/all teams using Serverless in some capacity, directly unblocking tight-interval scheduled jobs.

achievements.Title: Self-Service ML Platform CI/CD Shared Library (mlp-cicd)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: ML Platform and Global Data teams relied on a fragmented mix of Bamboo, Artifactory, and sprawling GitOps Jenkins pipelines to deploy Terraform infrastructure, Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs), Python libraries, and containers. Pipeline sprawl forced teams to maintain boilerplate CI/CD code, created inconsistent security/authentication patterns, and drove heavy manual ClickOps overhead.
achievements.Action: I led a 3-engineer task force to architect and build mlp-cicd, an org-wide Jenkins Shared Library written in Groovy and Python delivering turnkey and customizable CI/CD automation across Terraform deployments, Databricks DABs (scaled across Data Science and Data Engineering via workflow template repositories), Python library publishing, and container building/hosting. I owned the overall systems and implementation architecture—decoupling application repositories from underlying CI/CD plumbing, centralizing scoped authentication, and designing modular pipeline primitives—while delegating component and pipeline implementations across the task force.
achievements.Result: Enabled the Global Data organization (hundreds of engineers and data scientists) with self-service CI/CD automation—adopted across ~40 repositories, 100+ pipelines, and ~10 teams—reclaiming ~20% of engineering capacity relative to the sprawling GitOps baseline through a ~90% reduction in ClickOps and a ~20% reduction in SDLC iteration time.

achievements.Title: Platform Infrastructure Strategy & Terraform Refactor (MLPIP:Terraform)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: The Terraform codebase inherited at ML Platform team inception—managing AWS networking, storage, IAM, and secrets alongside Databricks workspaces, Unity Catalog securables, service principals, and cluster policies—was sparse, overly complex, non-DRY, and suffered from pattern sprawl and lack of environment parity, making it increasingly unmaintainable and blocking transient dev environments.
achievements.Action: I authored a strategic ADR and technical plan (MLPIP:Terraform) to re-architect our IaC around business-modeled hierarchical deployment layers (Cloud Account Infrastructure Seed, Data Lake Services, Databricks Workspaces, and Platform Data Assets). I standardized resource modularization, repository structure, branching and naming/addressing conventions, automated static analysis (tflint, terraform-docs, Make), local Dev Container ergonomics, and consistent module interfaces that made AI-assisted IaC development predictable and safe.
achievements.Result: Achieved 100% automated provisioning for transient platform environments, restored environment parity across AWS and Databricks infrastructure, and established structured repo and module conventions that standardized AI-assisted development workflows across the team.

achievements.Title: Cross-Cloud Tagging Enforcement & Cost Transparency
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: With hundreds of users across multiple teams deploying workloads on the ML Platform, combined resource tag completeness and coverage sat below ~30%, making it nearly impossible to determine resource ownership or accurately attribute cloud spend across AWS and Databricks.
achievements.Action: I designed and implemented a multi-layered tagging enforcement strategy spanning Databricks compute and AWS networking—combining native guardrails (Databricks Cluster Policies and Serverless Budget Policies) with framework-level enforcement through Jenkins CI/CD delegation and standardized Terraform/DABs module interfaces. To bring legacy resources into compliance without disrupting active teams, I remediated shared Terraform modules and configurations with consistent tagging patterns and integrated the resulting metadata into CloudZero.
achievements.Result: Raised cross-cloud financial and operational visibility from ~<30% to 95%+ across thousands of platform resources, giving teams granular cost attribution and workload performance-tuning visibility in CloudZero for the first time.

achievements.Title: Multi-Package Platform Python SDK (mlp-sdk)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Data science and ML teams had no straightforward way to run automated integration tests against Databricks—causing most teams to skip integration testing altogether—while sparse secrets-management patterns prevented self-service access and drove recurring operational support toil onto the platform team.
achievements.Action: I architected mlp-sdk, a multi-package Python monorepo built with uv, pytest, and ty and published to Artifactory via Jenkins. Using distinct namespaces and isolated package boundaries, I enabled teams to cherry-pick only the scoped capabilities they needed—including core runtime utilities, self-service secrets management, AWS authentication helpers, and automated pre-merge Databricks integration testing primitives.
achievements.Result: Adopted by ~5–6 teams across the ML Platform, establishing the organization's inaugural pre-merge Databricks integration testing lifecycle, standardizing self-service secrets access, improving data product stability, and reclaiming platform team operational capacity.

achievements.Title: Low-Code "Kickstarter" Workflow Template Ecosystem
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Onboarding a new Databricks workflow across DraftKings' 300+ user Global Analytics organization previously took months due to heavy reliance on DE/platform tickets, complex tenant authentication setup, and a steep learning curve across Databricks Asset Bundles (DABs) and CI/CD tooling.
achievements.Action: Partnering directly with ~6 Analytics teams, I architected a modular 'Kickstarter' workflow template ecosystem that bundled everything needed out of the box: a tenanted DABs repository structure, codified Authentication Scope tenant wiring, sample SQL/Python jobs and bundles, pre-wired Jenkins CI/CD pipelines, Dev Containers and Dev Container Features for local-to-CI parity, and standardized package management and dev tooling.
achievements.Result: Democratized Databricks workload development for the 300+ user Global Analytics organization—adopted across ~6 partner teams—and slashed 'time-to-first-insight' from months to days for non-technical and analytics stakeholders.

achievements.Title: Modular Dev Container Features & Agentic AI Tooling
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Engineers across the Data Science organization individually managed their own local development setups, creating chronic drift between local machines and CI/CD automation while forcing new hires to spend hours configuring runtimes, cloud credentials, CLIs, and AI coding tools.
achievements.Action: I architected a catalog of composable Dev Container Features published to Artifactory, allowing engineers to declaratively inject standardized containerized runtimes, platform CLIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) tooling, and pre-packaged agentic AI utilities (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Copilot). To eliminate manual auth configuration, I implemented automated cloud credential brokering via Dev Container Feature host mounts so installing a feature automatically projected host credentials cleanly into the container environment.
achievements.Result: Cut new-hire local environment setup time from hours to minutes, eliminated cross-platform local-to-CI divergence across the Data Science organization, and standardized agentic AI developer workflows out of the box.

achievements.Title: Policy-as-Code CI/CD Schema Validation Layer
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Across a 600+ user ML Platform, production workloads were frequently deployed without required cost and ownership tags or consistent service principal standards, creating attribution blind spots and governance drift that manual reviews could not catch at scale.
achievements.Action: I engineered a Policy-as-Code validation and enforcement layer combining CI/CD schema validation with Databricks Cluster Policies enforced directly at the Databricks API layer, causing non-compliant workload deployments missing mandatory cost/ownership metadata or service principal standards to fail fast before reaching production.
achievements.Result: Enforced 100% compliance across participating workloads (~20 repositories and ~50 pipelines) within the 600+ user platform, preventing untagged or non-compliant compute configurations from entering production and strengthening platform-wide FinOps attribution.

achievements.Title: Unified Identity Governance ("Authentication Scopes")
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Onboarding a new ML Platform tenant previously involved chaotic, inconsistent manual provisioning of fragmented identity resources across AWS, Databricks, Entra ID, and Jenkins—creating heavy developer cognitive load, inconsistent permission boundaries, and operational toil.
achievements.Action: I architected 'Authentication Scopes', a unified business-level Terraform abstraction that harmonized multi-system identity lifecycle management into a single declarative construct. Provisioning one Authentication Scope automatically created and wired the tenant's full identity stack—including Databricks Service Principals, Unity Catalog Service Credentials, AWS IAM Roles and Role Policies, Secrets Manager namespaces, Entra ID bindings, and isolated Jenkins Folders.
achievements.Result: Eliminated cross-system IAM fragmentation and reduced developer cognitive load, reaching ~60% adoption across platform users (~20 teams) while continuing to scale organization-wide as the standard tenancy pattern.

achievements.Title: Python Execution Runtime Stability & Pinning
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Engineers ran Python workloads across three separate environments—local workstations, Jenkins CI/CD runners, and managed Databricks production runtimes—with frequent dependency and runtime drift causing recurring environment-specific bugs between local development and production.
achievements.Action: I designed and implemented a runtime stability pattern that mirrored official Databricks Runtimes inside project Dev Containers paired with strict uv package pinning. I then wired Jenkins CI/CD pipelines to execute static analysis, unit/integration testing, and deployment workflows inside those exact project Dev Containers so every stage ran against an identical runtime contract.
achievements.Result: Adopted across ~5–10 repositories and ~20 engineers, delivering consistent local-to-CI-to-production parity while preserving Databricks-managed production runtimes and improving both local developer ergonomics and Python application reliability.

achievements.Title: Platform Team Project Management & Agile Transformation
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: When the ML Platform team launched (scaling from 2 to 8 engineers), it inherited heavy Scrum ceremonies and workflows from Data Engineering (~5 hours/week in ceremonies) that clashed with exploratory platform engineering work, creating process friction where engineers spent more time talking about work than building.
achievements.Action: I partnered with team leadership to redesign our Jira and Confluence operating model into a lightweight, self-organizing hybrid blending Kanban, Scrum, and structured Waterfall concepts—trimming recurring standup ceremonies, establishing single-point initiative ownership, mirroring Kanban flow, prioritizing backlogs, and adding issue templates, democratized story pointing, ideation sagas, and ticket tagging.
achievements.Result: Cut weekly ceremony overhead by ~40% (~2 hours/week saved per engineer, down from ~5 hours/week) as the team scaled from 2 to 8 engineers, improving engineering focus, ownership clarity, and day-to-day velocity.

achievements.Title: Stakeholder Engagement via ML@DK User Series
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: ML Platform consumers previously interacted with Platform Engineers almost exclusively through reactive troubleshooting threads in a public Slack channel, leaving no structured, proactive forum for sharing platform roadmaps, architecture patterns, or gathering structured user feedback.
achievements.Action: Alongside fellow platform engineers and team leadership, I co-launched and drove the monthly ML@DK User Series—a recurring org-wide evangelism and enablement forum covering platform roadmap priorities, feature releases, architectural deep dives, live Q&A, and open customer feedback documented in Confluence.
achievements.Result: Built a consistent monthly engagement channel reaching ~70 ML, data science, and analytics stakeholders per session, strengthening two-way roadmap visibility, platform awareness, and user trust across the organization.

achievements.Title: Cross-Org ML Platform Architecture Consulting
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: At ML Platform inauguration, core architectural foundations suffered from poor maintainability and scalability, yet key dependencies spanned multiple partner organizations—including Global Architecture, Site Reliability, Platform Services, and Data Platform—requiring influence without direct authority.
achievements.Action: Drawing on 5+ years of production Databricks platform engineering experience, I served as an architectural advisor across partner teams, driving consensus on foundational platform-engineering patterns across Data Architecture (Unity Catalog structure), Environment Architecture (workspace and data environment isolation), Model and Data Asset Lifecycle governance, and AWS network topology and security boundaries.
achievements.Result: Aligned Global Architecture, SRE, Platform Services, and Data Platform around a cohesive, maintainable ML Platform blueprint, establishing clear multi-team architectural decisions for catalog structure, environment separation, and asset lifecycle governance.

achievements.Title: Legacy CI/CD Migration (Octo/Bamboo to GitOps Jenkins)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: The ML Platform team's build-and-release pipelines relied on legacy Bamboo and Octopus Deploy (Octo) tooling that Platform Services was actively deprecating and no longer supporting for new deployment patterns—directly blocking the team from provisioning new ML Platform development environments.
achievements.Action: I led the migration of ~6 core ML Platform repositories off Bamboo and Octopus Deploy onto DraftKings' internally managed GitOps Jenkins Framework built by Platform Services, refactoring Terraform and AWS deployment pipelines onto the supported infrastructure foundation.
achievements.Result: Unblocked ML Platform development environment provisioning, improved deployment reliability and flexibility across ~6 core repositories, and established the underlying Jenkins infrastructure that later enabled a smooth evolution to Vanilla Jenkins and the org-wide Shared Library.

achievements.Title: Lead Engineering Technical & Leadership Hiring
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: The ML Platform team launched with just two engineers (including myself) facing rapid enterprise demand across hundreds of ML and analytics stakeholders, while inherited hiring loops lacked calibrated technical and leadership evaluation standards tailored to platform engineering.
achievements.Action: I partnered with leadership to rethink and redesign the team's entire hiring process—overhauling both technical assessments (using HackerRank and practical architecture evaluation) and behavioral/leadership rubrics documented in Confluence—and served as a core interviewer in a democratic hiring loop for Lead and Senior ML Platform candidates via Workday.
achievements.Result: Helped scale the ML Platform team 4x from 2 to 8 engineers while raising hiring calibration, diversifying technical depth, and multiplying team delivery bandwidth across DraftKings.

achievements.Title: Platform Compute Infrastructure & Management Strategy
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Across 600+ Databricks users and 20+ teams on the ML Platform, teams needed elastic self-service compute spanning classic clusters, instance pools, and serverless—but ad-hoc, inconsistent compute configurations across teams and environments created governance sprawl, poor instance pool utilization, right-sizing gaps, and opaque cost ownership.
achievements.Action: I designed and implemented a unified platform compute infrastructure and management strategy codified in Terraform with Entra ID group integration, standardizing how clusters, instance pools, and serverless resources were provisioned and governed via Databricks cluster policies, serverless budget policies, and scoped permission grants.
achievements.Result: Standardized self-service compute governance across 600+ Databricks users and 20+ teams, reducing configuration complexity while improving compute right-sizing, instance pool utilization, and cost/ownership attribution.

achievements.Title: Standardized Platform Monitoring & Alerting (Datadog)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: ML Platform workloads—including Databricks Workflows and Model Serving endpoints—had 0% standardized platform monitoring and alerting, leaving teams blind to production performance regressions, inflating incident Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), and risking runaway Datadog log-ingestion costs from unfiltered cluster telemetry.
achievements.Action: I architected and rolled out an end-to-end observability stack codified in Terraform, Python, Spark, and Bash: configuring native Datadog-Databricks integrations, building a Spark streaming job exporting custom telemetry to AWS S3 for Datadog ingestion, customizing the standard Datadog cluster agent install init script to enforce implied cluster tags while scoping/limiting collected logs, and wiring Databricks Notification Destinations for platform administration alerting.
achievements.Result: Expanded Databricks Job and Model Serving monitoring coverage from 0% to 100% with 'out-of-the-box' extensible observability, saved ~$30k+/year in Datadog log-ingestion costs via scoped log collection, and enabled faster outage triage and job performance tuning across teams.

achievements.Title: ML Platform Data Masking Solution
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: DraftKings' data architecture embedded PII inside shared tables that non-elevated users also needed to query, creating a governance requirement to mask sensitive columns selectively so broader teams could access safe views of those tables.
achievements.Action: I built a declarative Databricks job framework backed by YAML masking policy configurations stored in Git, automatically applying static Unity Catalog column-masking functions to target tables and columns to give teams a self-service masking mechanism.
achievements.Result: Delivered working self-serve Unity Catalog column masking adopted across a handful of schemas, though real-world adoption remained low because static YAML-and-job configuration proved too cumbersome for teams to maintain—providing an instructive product lesson on minimizing DevEx friction in governance tooling.

achievements.Title: Platform Development & Test Environment Architecture Consulting
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Across DraftKings' data and ML ecosystems, teams lacked true development environments due to a structural mismatch between engineering environments and data environments, widespread confusion between an 'environment' and an 'instance', and a broken end-to-end data-asset SDLC (such as needing to load-test real ML models in environments that lacked access to realistic data).
achievements.Action: I partnered with Data Architecture to analyze the root conceptual misalignment and proposed a simplified dev/test/prod environment architecture incorporating embedded application instances (for specialized workloads like research and load testing) rather than proliferating separate, inconsistent environments for each use case.
achievements.Result: Delivered a clear architectural blueprint clarifying environment-vs-instance boundaries and end-to-end data/model SDLC paths; although organizational bureaucracy prevented formal adoption and the underlying environment gaps persisted, the proposal sharpened cross-org awareness of the architectural root causes.

achievements.Title: Standardized Platform Compute Tagging (Datadog Init Scripts)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Even after enabling the native Datadog-Databricks integration for platform-wide visibility, individual teams struggled to locate and filter their own compute metrics in Datadog because clusters lacked consistent, automatically captured workload tags.
achievements.Action: I engineered custom Bash cluster init scripts that read Databricks-generated Spark configuration files at runtime to automatically extract implied platform tags while supporting extensible team-defined custom tags. I embedded the init scripts inherently via Terraform-managed Databricks Compute Policies so every cluster received standardized tagging automatically.
achievements.Result: Took every team on the ML Platform from zero to full searchable compute observability overnight, empowering teams across the organization to build custom workload dashboards and alerts directly on top of tagged Datadog metrics and logs.

achievements.Title: SharedLibrary CI/CD Observability (mlp-cicd Telemetry)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Dozens of teams relied daily on mlp-cicd Jenkins Shared Library functions for mission-critical SDLC and DevOps workflows, yet the platform team had 0% observability into which teams consumed which library versions, which atomic functions failed most often, or whether library updates silently broke downstream pipelines.
achievements.Action: I architected and implemented a heavily abstracted telemetry layer inside mlp-cicd using direct Datadog API calls authenticated through the existing Datadog Jenkins plugin/daemon. The abstraction made instrumenting any new capability, customized atomic function, or pipeline trivial, capturing consumer identity, library usage, atomic function errors, and end-to-end pipeline failures automatically.
achievements.Result: Scaled SharedLibrary observability from 0% to 100% usage coverage overnight across thousands of weekly pipeline executions and dozens of consuming teams, enabling data-driven product prioritization, proactive regression detection, and faster troubleshooting of user issues.

achievements.Title: Global Data Platform Unified IAM & Governance via ConductorOne (GDP IAM - C1)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: Global Data Platform (GDP) engineering teams—both Data and ML—were continually bogged down fulfilling access and governance requests either slowly through Terraform SDLC changes or manually via Snowflake SQL commands. Worse, platform engineers were not the actual data owners and lacked business context to judge whether access should be granted, while fragmented IAM models across AWS, Databricks, Snowflake, and Jenkins created operational chaos.
achievements.Action: I architected the unified distributed IAM and governance platform integrating ConductorOne across the entire GDP ecosystem (AWS, Databricks, Snowflake, Jenkins, Entra ID, and Okta). I designed the end-to-end operating architecture: Terraform resource provisioning, canonical access groups, group-to-resource mappings, access profiles, delegated data-owner approval routing inside ConductorOne, and automated grant propagation from ConductorOne groups into all integrated GDP applications.
achievements.Result: Unified access governance across 600+ GDP users and dozens of data teams (within an enterprise footprint spanning thousands of DraftKings users), returning governance ownership to real data owners, accelerating access turnaround up to near-instantaneous for low-risk grants, delivering auditable compliance, slashing platform ops toil, and harmonizing cross-system IAM (such as shared Databricks and Snowflake governance).

achievements.Title: DraftKings Internal Knowledge Hub / Wiki (Gyrus Fork)
achievements.Role: Senior ML Platform Engineer & Technical Lead
achievements.Challenge: DraftKings suffered from sparse, stale, and unmaintained documentation across traditional hubs like Confluence, leaving both human engineers and AI coding agents without trustworthy institutional context for knowledge discovery, architecture design, or implementation.
achievements.Action: I forked my personal Gyrus knowledge platform to build a self-sufficient, DraftKings-specific internal Knowledge Hub and Git-backed wiki (gyrus/wiki). To make adoption seamless inside DraftKings' environment, I adapted and hosted the full supporting stack: the Go-based Gyrus CLI and MCP server, an internal AI Marketplace for AI plugin distribution across Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, and Antigravity, Go dev/CI containers built via Jenkins and Artifactory, PostgreSQL persistence, and a Dev Container Feature for one-step team distribution.
achievements.Result: Adopted across 100% of the ML Platform team's SDLC (~8 engineers) and became the foundational knowledge layer powering downstream platform products—including an internal feature explorer/development tool (glossary and dev context) and 'Smokey', an automated firefighter AI agent that surfaced wiki knowledge and opened PRs on behalf of requesting users, indirectly extending wiki value across the entire ML Platform userbase.

achievements.Title: Scalable Hub-and-Spoke Databricks Workspace Mesh
achievements.Challenge: As part of VUMC's Unity Catalog initiative, 100+ heavily containerized Databricks workspaces (deployed with managed VNet injection) needed to operate like a mesh network for secure cross-department data sharing. The existing Azure network topology could not support workspace-to-workspace communication without destructive rebuilds or permanent data loss, and Databricks' vendor-proposed alternative was both overly complex and cost-prohibitive.
achievements.Action: I evaluated the network constraints and architected a Terraform-managed Hub-and-Spoke network topology designed to roll out once workspace persistence was decoupled, enforcing strict tenant isolation via Azure Private Link. To eliminate manual networking toil, I designed a programmatic CIDR lookup pattern at Terraform plan/apply time to allocate available IP ranges from pre-determined blocks for VNet peering, and routed egress domain filtering through a single centralized platform firewall rather than per-workspace firewalls.
achievements.Result: Delivered the production architecture and implementation blueprint enabling secure peer-to-peer data sharing across 100+ Databricks workspaces while projecting $200k+ in annual savings by consolidating domain filtering onto a centralized firewall (planned and handed off prior to my departure from VUMC).

achievements.Title: Zero-Trust External Data Platform (Isolake)
achievements.Challenge: VUMC needed to collaborate with external medical centers on sensitive healthcare and PHI-adjacent research datasets, but strict HIPAA compliance and institutional governance required VUMC to retain absolute control over what data entered or left the cloud perimeter at all times.
achievements.Action: I architected and built Isolake, a zero-trust Trusted Research Environment (clean-room data lake) hosted inside VUMC's Azure perimeter using Azure Bicep abstractions and unidirectional Azure Private Links. All data ingress and egress operated strictly as VUMC-administered push/pull workflows isolated from the core enterprise data lake, while external researchers interacted exclusively through a locked-down Databricks Workspace running on VUMC-owned infrastructure so raw data could not be exfiltrated.
achievements.Result: Scaled VUMC's secure multi-institution data reach from 1 to 28 medical centers, unlocking participation in a vastly larger collaborative clinical research data pool while maintaining HIPAA-compliant zero-trust network isolation.

achievements.Title: Enterprise Terraform Migration & Brownfield Automation
achievements.Challenge: The VUMC Data Platform managed 30,000+ cloud resources via Azure Bicep and PowerShell, but rolling out Unity Catalog and managing Databricks workspaces uniformly required multi-provider IaC capabilities that Bicep could not natively cover without brittle scripting.
achievements.Action: I led the architectural design and drove a 2–3 engineer migration effort transitioning the 30,000+ Azure and Databricks resource estate onto a unified Terraform ecosystem, paired with a serverless Python Terraform client API backed by remote cloud state and scoped IAM roles. To adopt massive brownfield infrastructure cleanly without downtime, I engineered custom GitLab CI automation for implied infrastructure imports using a hidden .imports.tf file in the root configuration directory (gracefully no-oping when absent) that refreshed and imported existing resources automatically before terraform plan.
achievements.Result: Established a unified, multi-provider IaC architecture and zero-downtime brownfield import pipeline spanning 30,000+ Azure and Databricks resources, simplifying toolchain complexity and enabling broader team participation in infrastructure development (migration execution continued with the team after my departure).

achievements.Title: Azure Blob Storage Tier Lifecycle Management
achievements.Challenge: As the VUMC Delta Lake platform ingested growing volumes of historical clinical and operational data, Azure Blob Storage spend began scaling at an exponential rate, threatening long-term platform sustainability.
achievements.Action: I performed storage access-pattern research tailored to Delta Lake table files and ran trial cost models to verify that Azure-managed backend lifecycle tiering could safely transition aging blobs across storage tiers without incurring unexpected operational penalties. I then codified native Azure Blob Storage lifecycle management policies using Azure Bicep to automate tiering across the lakehouse.
achievements.Result: Immediately reduced the platform's storage cost growth trajectory and delivered ~$50k in annual savings at the initial implementation snapshot, with savings compounding as dataset volumes continued to expand.

achievements.Title: Delta Lake Retention & Archival Pipeline
achievements.Challenge: Even after native Azure Blob lifecycle tiering slowed immediate storage spend, rapid Delta Lake table version accumulation continued driving unsustainable storage volume growth across the enterprise lakehouse.
achievements.Action: I designed and implemented automated Delta Lake retention and archival pipelines driven by data-asset metadata. Table-level retention properties were governed declaratively through metadata and enforced by automated VACUUM runs embedded in ingestion pipeline processing, while historical table versions required for compliance were archived to separate cold storage via Delta DEEP CLONE jobs.
achievements.Result: Flattened platform storage accumulation from an exponential curve to a logarithmic trajectory, realizing ~$140k in annual savings at the implementation snapshot with compounding cost avoidance over time.

achievements.Title: Point-in-Time Data Asset Reconstruction Engine (CDC)
achievements.Challenge: Maintaining separate Delta Lake archival jobs and long-term cloned snapshots still carried meaningful storage costs and operational complexity, yet clinical and enterprise governance required 100% point-in-time data recoverability.
achievements.Action: Recognizing that our extraction and ingestion pipelines already captured full execution context alongside raw persisted CDC/extraction data, I engineered a custom point-in-time reconstruction engine in Python and Spark that re-executed historical pipeline context to rebuild any Delta table as of any prior timestamp on demand. I intentionally traded rare ad-hoc compute spend—treating rebuilt outputs as ad-hoc snapshots rather than mutating the live source of truth—in exchange for permanently lower storage spend, and validated end-to-end reconstruction across real platform assets.
achievements.Result: Eliminated separate archival pipelines and archival storage completely while maintaining validated 100% data recoverability and full Delta Lake capabilities, generating an estimated $200k+ in annual storage savings at snapshot (compounding over time).

achievements.Title: Self-Service Data Asset Observability Platform (Lake-Ops)
achievements.Challenge: Clinical researchers, developers, and platform admins had no self-service way to see when upstream data assets finished refreshing or whether ingestion pipelines were healthy, causing recurring manual status inquiries (~several pings per week to the product manager) and downstream scheduling delays.
achievements.Action: I architected and built Lake-Ops, a decoupled full-stack Progressive Web App pairing a serverless Python/FastAPI backend service with a static .NET Blazor WebAssembly frontend over a SQL Server persistence layer to track extraction and ingestion lifecycles in near real time.
achievements.Result: Empowered 30+ researchers, developers, and admins with self-service visibility into platform data asset state and health, eliminating recurring manual status reporting to product management and laying the foundation for event-driven orchestration.

achievements.Title: Resilient Serverless Delegated Extraction Gateway
achievements.Challenge: While Azure Data Factory (ADF) handled standard source connectors well, complex external and internal APIs—including Workday SOAP endpoints and heavily rate-limited, authenticated, deeply paginated REST APIs—exceeded native ADF capabilities and caused out-of-memory (OOM) failures and partial data loss.
achievements.Action: I architected a resilient serverless Python delegated extraction gateway built on Azure Durable Functions invoked seamlessly by ADF. I engineered a dynamic chunking engine and stateful orchestration recovery layer that automated intelligent pagination, authentication handoffs, and exponential backoff while giving engineers an idiomatic Python interface for onboarding custom API connectors.
achievements.Result: Enabled 40+ complex public, internal, SOAP, and rate-limited API integrations with zero OOM failures or data loss, expanding platform ingestion coverage well beyond standard cloud connector limits.

achievements.Title: Standardized Hierarchical Development Container Repository
achievements.Challenge: Platform engineers developed across mixed operating systems (Mac, Linux, Windows) and CPU architectures (ARM and x86) while maintaining ~10 repositories targeting shared Databricks Spark runtimes, leading to duplicated Dockerfiles, subtle local-vs-production drift, and redundant CI/CD image rebuilds.
achievements.Action: I architected a hierarchical Docker container image repository published to GitLab Registry that mirrored official Databricks Spark runtimes as a single DRY base hierarchy for Dev Containers and CI pipelines. I paired the hierarchy with on-change GitLab CI build automation so only modified image layers rebuilt during updates.
achievements.Result: Achieved 100% environment parity across local development, CI/CD, and production, adopted by every developer on the platform team across all ~10 platform repositories while eliminating cross-platform runtime friction and reducing redundant CI build overhead.

achievements.Title: Serverless Platform Administration Gateway API
achievements.Challenge: Because the Data Platform ran within a single Azure subscription, platform admins previously needed elevated direct Azure permissions to deploy or manage cloud resources, creating excessive privilege exposure and requiring admins to understand low-level IaC internals for routine operations.
achievements.Action: I architected a serverless Python/FastAPI REST API gateway running on Azure Functions that executed IaC (Azure Bicep and later Terraform) on behalf of platform admins via tightly scoped IAM roles. The API abstracted low-level provisioning mechanics behind high-level business endpoints, serving both our internal Admin Toolkit UI and direct programmatic callers.
achievements.Result: Enforced the Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)—eliminating elevated direct Azure privileges for end-users and admins—while centralizing and standardizing provisioning across 6 core platform deployments.

achievements.Title: Internal Python Frameworks & Shared Library Ecosystem
achievements.Challenge: The Data Platform team operated multiple production services across overlapping concerns—including Microsoft Teams webhook/card notifications, API authentication, serverless applications, and pipeline job graphs—creating growing risk of architectural divergence, duplicated boilerplate, and high maintenance overhead across repositories.
achievements.Action: I engineered a reusable suite of internal Python libraries and a serverless application framework published to GitLab Registry and Azure Storage. The libraries standardized cross-cutting primitives—including Credential Scoping, Inversion of Control (IoC) service injection, job-graph orchestration patterns, and Microsoft Teams card/webhook alerting—so teams could compose new services on a shared DRY foundation.
achievements.Result: Adopted across 6+ mission-critical platform products, eliminating cross-repository architectural drift and substantially improving service maintainability and developer efficiency when standing up new applications.

achievements.Title: Enterprise IaC Evangelism & Terraform Teaching
achievements.Challenge: While the Data Platform team managed 30,000+ Azure resources through Terraform and automated GitLab CI brownfield imports, many peer teams across VUMC IT still relied on manual cloud provisioning and lacked a clear blueprint for adopting IaC at enterprise scale.
achievements.Action: I prepared and delivered a technical talk at the VUMC technical conference to ~50 engineers and IT practitioners, walking through our scalable Terraform architecture, state-management practices, and automated CI/CD import workflows to lay out a practical roadmap for bringing legacy cloud environments under code-defined governance.
achievements.Result: Raised institutional awareness of modern IaC patterns across ~50 VUMC IT stakeholders, demonstrating a proven, production-tested pathway for migrating brownfield Azure infrastructure into governed Terraform pipelines.

achievements.Title: Multi-Tenant Research Grant Back-Billing Analytics
achievements.Challenge: Dozens of VUMC departments and individual clinical research groups operated on the shared Data Platform under strictly audited research grants, creating an urgent need to accurately attribute multi-tenant storage, network, compute, and Databricks expenditures back to specific cost centers.
achievements.Action: I architected a multi-tenant FinOps cost attribution engine and Databricks analytics dashboard combining a cell-based compute isolation model with a custom Python/Spark analytics pipeline ingesting Azure Blob Inventory logs alongside compute and network billing data into Delta Lake.
achievements.Result: Delivered 100% auditability for multi-tenant cloud expenditures, automating monthly back-billing across dozens of VUMC cost centers representing tens of thousands of dollars per month in attributed cloud spend.

achievements.Title: Unified Data Governance Architecture (Unity Catalog)
achievements.Challenge: VUMC previously relied on fragmented per-workspace Hive Metastores and custom sync scripts to expose 8,000+ data assets across 100+ Databricks workspaces and 130+ source systems, creating brittle maintenance overhead and blocking newer Unity Catalog features—while active clinical and enterprise consumers required zero downtime during migration.
achievements.Action: I architected a centralized Unity Catalog multi-environment governance hierarchy deployed alongside the legacy Hive Metastore to execute a zero-downtime cutover. I structured environments at the top-level catalog boundary so workloads could swap cleanly between dev and prod using USE CATALOG without hardcoded paths, and automated identity and group lifecycle governance through Entra ID SCIM synchronization managed via Terraform.
achievements.Result: Modernized governance across 8,000+ assets, 130+ source systems, and 100+ workspaces with zero downtime, retiring brittle metastore sync scripts, improving developer ergonomics, and unblocking Unity Catalog-dependent platform capabilities.

achievements.Title: Multi-Arch CI/CD Runner & Hybrid-Cloud Modernization
achievements.Challenge: The Data Platform managed on-prem GitLab CI/CD runner VMs stuck on RHEL 7 alongside Azure Data Factory Integration Runtimes, preventing Docker upgrades needed for modern Python and Databricks runtime images. Simultaneously, ARM64/AMD64 hardware mismatches stretched local container build cycles to 25 minutes across the ~10-engineer platform team.
achievements.Action: I upgraded the runner VMs to RHEL 9, migrated container builds from deprecated Docker to RHEL-supported Podman aliased seamlessly as docker, and introduced a multi-architecture (ARM64/AMD64) container build strategy. During rollout, I dove deep into host-level container virtual networking to diagnose and resolve systemic networking conflicts caused by VUMC IT's default VM firewall configurations.
achievements.Result: Accelerated local developer environment build cycles by 80% (from 25 minutes to 5 minutes) for ~10 platform engineers and unblocked CI/CD builds for newer Python versions and modern Databricks container runtimes.

achievements.Title: Geospatial Address Deduplication & Geocoding Engine
achievements.Challenge: Clinical researchers needed geocoded addresses across millions of patient and clinic records to study spatial disease correlations and power clinic recommendations, but commercial turn-key geocoding APIs were prohibitively expensive—especially with duplicate and inconsistently formatted addresses inflating call volumes.
achievements.Action: I researched, architected, and implemented an in-house distributed geospatial deduplication and geocoding engine on Databricks using SparkSQL and Python, applying a weighted Levenshtein string-distance fuzzy-matching algorithm that evaluated billions of cross-join candidate pairs to isolate unique normalized address assets prior to any external API lookups.
achievements.Result: Achieved >90% exact geocoding accuracy (approaching commercial turn-key quality) across millions of addresses, avoiding an estimated ~$5k+ in third-party geocoding API costs and unlocking organization-wide geospatial clinical analytics.

achievements.Title: Enterprise MLOps & Production Model Serving Strategy
achievements.Challenge: Although VUMC operated a mature Azure Databricks data lakehouse for BI and research, it had zero production MLOps or model serving infrastructure—preventing clinical researchers from promoting high-impact models (such as predicting and reducing unnecessary pre-surgery blood testing) into enterprise clinical applications.
achievements.Action: I designed and implemented VUMC's inaugural enterprise MLOps ecosystem and model SDLC strategy on Azure Databricks, codifying technical governance, Unity Catalog Model Registry / MLflow workflows, environment abstractions for structured dev -> prod promotion, and Terraform-backed Databricks Model Serving endpoints.
achievements.Result: Enabled production ML model serving at VUMC for the first time, realizing $500k+ in indirect annual value from a single launched clinical use case while unlocking a multi-million-dollar projected pipeline of additional research models.

achievements.Title: Dynamic WSDL-to-Spark Schema Interpreter
achievements.Challenge: Ingesting full enterprise datasets from VUMC's Workday SOAP API involved ~6 heavily nested object endpoints—such as Worker objects containing hundreds of nested attributes across tens of millions of records—making manual Spark schema authoring a slow, error-prone multi-day bottleneck per object.
achievements.Action: I engineered a dynamic Python WSDL-to-Spark schema interpreter integrated directly into the core Extraction API, enabling 'Just-In-Time' XML/WSDL schema discovery and automated type mapping into Delta-compatible SparkSchemas at runtime without hand-coded schema definitions.
achievements.Result: Reduced data onboarding latency for complex Workday SOAP objects by 95% (from days to minutes) across ~6 deeply nested endpoints spanning tens of millions of records, establishing a self-describing integration layer that eliminated ongoing manual schema maintenance.

achievements.Title: End-to-End Platform Asset Cost Management Analytics
achievements.Challenge: Across 130+ integrated source systems and 8,000+ managed data assets, the cost to materialize and retain individual datasets varied sharply by integration cadence and storage footprint. Unlike user/cost-center back-billing, the platform team lacked per-asset cost visibility to identify expensive tables that were underutilized or no longer actively consumed.
achievements.Action: I built an end-to-end per-asset cost management analytics solution in Databricks (SQL, Spark, and Delta Lake) that quantified the true compute and storage cost of materializing and storing each individual data asset and table across the platform.
achievements.Result: Armed the Data Platform team with granular per-table unit economics to tune retention versions and optimize integration strategies for low-usage assets, yielding estimated annual savings in the tens of thousands of dollars.

achievements.Title: Metadata-Driven Ingestion Engine (Guzzler)
achievements.Challenge: Previously, onboarding each new source system or dataset onto VUMC's data lake required building and maintaining bespoke per-asset pipelines, creating unsustainable engineering toil as institutional demand grew toward thousands of datasets.
achievements.Action: Joining slightly after inception, I co-architected Guzzler—a metadata-driven Python and Spark ingestion engine integrated with Azure Data Factory, SQL Server, and GitLab CI. Using Strategy and Factory design patterns backed by schema-enforced JSON configurations, we enabled zero-code dataset onboarding and automated schema evolution across all standard enterprise data formats.
achievements.Result: Scaled to support 8,000+ data assets across 130+ source systems while collapsing new dataset onboarding from bespoke pipeline builds to a declarative JSON metadata pull request fulfilled and merged in ~1 hour.

achievements.Title: Data Pipeline Application (Guzzler) Presentation & Teaching
achievements.Challenge: Even as VUMC's custom Guzzler ingestion engine scaled to thousands of data assets, downstream engineers and organizational stakeholders lacked clear visibility into how the ingestion architecture operated or what onboarding capabilities the platform could support.
achievements.Action: Serving as subject matter expert and co-architect/lead developer of Guzzler, I organized and delivered an architectural walkthrough and product-evangelism presentation to ~30 engineers and stakeholders covering the engine's metadata-driven ingestion patterns, throughput capacity, and onboarding workflows.
achievements.Result: Built stronger cross-team awareness of Data Platform capabilities across ~30 engineers and stakeholders, demystifying ingestion architecture and driving broader organizational alignment around platform adoption.

achievements.Title: Platform Engineering Hiring & Junior Onboarding
achievements.Challenge: VUMC's lean Data Platform team (~6 engineers) faced accelerating enterprise demand and needed to grow its engineering bandwidth—particularly by hiring and ramping recent college graduates who lacked prior cloud or Databricks production experience before Databricks' formal academy resources had matured.
achievements.Action: As Tech Lead, I partnered with our engineering manager to conduct technical and cultural interviews with final hiring-recommendation sign-off. After hiring, I authored custom Databricks learning curricula, architectural walkthroughs, and project documentation to systematically onboard and mentor the new-grad engineers onto our platform stack.
achievements.Result: Expanded the Data Platform team by 25%+ (growing roughly from ~6 to ~9 engineers), multiplying team delivery and innovation bandwidth while accelerating junior hires into productive contributors.

achievements.Title: Cloud Admin Privilege Governance (Azure PIM)
achievements.Challenge: Within the Data Platform's dedicated Azure subscription, ~5 platform administrators held standing Global Admin privileges, creating unnecessary security exposure and elevated risk of accidental production or IAM mutations.
achievements.Action: I designed and rolled out Azure Privileged Identity Management (PIM) via Entra ID across the platform subscription, transitioning all ~5 administrators off standing Global Admin access onto audited, time-bound Just-in-Time (JIT) elevation gated by mandatory written justification and explicit approval workflows.
achievements.Result: Eliminated standing Global Admin privileges across ~5 platform administrators, hardening cloud IAM governance and sharply reducing accidental-change and security blast radius across VUMC's Data Platform subscription.

achievements.Title: Platform Administration Toolkit (PowerShell CLI)
achievements.Challenge: After building the Serverless Platform Administration Gateway API to execute delegated IaC deployments across Azure subscriptions, the ~6-person platform team had no dedicated operator interface—forcing engineers to manually craft and invoke raw HTTP requests for routine environment operations.
achievements.Action: I built a dedicated PowerShell CLI Administration Toolkit wrapping the serverless Azure Functions IaC gateway, giving platform operators clean, discoverable commands for invoking environment provisioning and administration workflows across Azure subscriptions.
achievements.Result: Improved day-to-day operator efficiency and DevEx for the ~6-person platform engineering team by replacing raw API calls with a consistent, low-friction PowerShell CLI interface.

achievements.Title: Azure Function Infrastructure Meta-Monitoring & Alerting
achievements.Challenge: VUMC's Data Platform relied on ~3–4 Azure Function Apps to power state management, monitoring, alerting, and data integrations—and experienced a blind-spot outage where the alerting Function App itself went down silently, failing to notify the team of downstream pipeline failures.
achievements.Action: I designed and implemented out-of-band infrastructure meta-monitoring ('watching the watchers') using Azure Monitor and Application Insights across all ~3–4 core Function Apps, routing infrastructure health-check failures directly via email as an independent fallback path decoupled from our primary Function-App alerting service.
achievements.Result: Eliminated silent monitoring blind spots across all ~3–4 mission-critical serverless applications, enabling rapid outage detection and response even when primary application-level alerting was unavailable.

achievements.Title: Geospatial Floorplan & Hospital Capacity Analytics
achievements.Challenge: At VUMC, physical floor space directly dictates hospital bed capacity (and patient volume) as well as research lab allocation, yet the space-utilization department had no scalable way to ingest architectural CAD floorplan data into the lakehouse or run spatial queries in Spark.
achievements.Action: I built a custom distributed Python geospatial ingestion pipeline distributing GeoPandas processing across Spark workers to transform CAD floorplan data into Delta Lake tables, and configured Databricks compute clusters with Apache Sedona JARs to expose scalable spatial SQL analytics to end users.
achievements.Result: Unlocked lakehouse-scale geospatial floorplan analytics across VUMC facilities, enabling data-driven optimization of hospital bed capacity and clinical research laboratory utilization.

achievements.Title: Original Enterprise Platform IaC Implementation (Azure Bicep)
achievements.Challenge: VUMC's Azure Databricks Delta Lakehouse and supporting backend services grew to 30,000+ cloud resources spanning 100+ workspaces and multiple environments, while existing infrastructure was managed via verbose, static ARM JSON templates deployed through CI/CD that were cumbersome to read, maintain, and scale across environments.
achievements.Action: I migrated and re-engineered the platform's foundational Infrastructure-as-Code estate from static ARM templates into modular, declarative Azure Bicep paired with PowerShell and GitLab CI automation, implementing reusable variable-driven configurations shared cleanly across all environments (later serving as the baseline for the multi-provider Terraform migration).
achievements.Result: Established a maintainable, variable-driven IaC foundation governing 30,000+ Azure resources and 100+ workspaces across all environments—improving deployment stability, security consistency, developer efficiency, and cloud cost governance.
